name: Reed Bingham State Park
unique: A blackwater river backed up into a 375 acre lake with cypress and tupelo standing in the water, plus one of the densest gopher tortoise populations in the state on the sand ridges above.
buzz: The lake swimming area and the canoe trail get the family traffic. The tortoise burrows along the trail are the thing people did not expect.

name: Cook County Historical Society Museum
unique: A WPA-era post office turned museum and genealogical library, with the county's farm and turpentine records, school photographs and family files open to anyone tracing a line through south Georgia.
buzz: The volunteers are the resource here and they know the county by name. Best for people with a reason to be in the files.

name: Adel Daylily Festival
unique: Adel grows and ships daylilies commercially, and the town throws a festival around the bloom with tubs of named cultivars for sale, a 5K and a car show on the courthouse streets.
buzz: Growers bring divisions you cannot buy at a box store. It is a plant person's morning more than a carnival.

name: Jefferson Davis Memorial State Historic Site
customer: Civil War readers, history road trippers
unique: The pine woods clearing where Jefferson Davis was taken in May 1865 wearing his wife's raincoat, marked by a Greek Revival colonnade built in the 1930s and a small museum with the story of the chase.
buzz: Quiet and odd, a monument to a lost cause raised by the state decades later. The museum explains the raid better than most battlefield signs.

name: Georgia Sweet Potato Festival
unique: More than sixty years of sweet potato pie contests, a parade and a queen, in the town that ships the crop out by the truckload every fall.
buzz: The pie contest is the real competition and the entries run out fast. Small, local and entirely itself.

name: Prater Music Fest
customer: Soul and R&B fans, locals, families
unique: A small town music festival named for Dave Prater, the Ocilla-born half of Sam and Dave, with southern soul and gospel acts on a stage downtown.
buzz: The Sam and Dave connection gives it more weight than a town festival usually has. Lineups are local and regional, and the crowd is there to dance.

name: Ocmulgee Wild Hog Festival
customer: Families, barbecue people, hog dog handlers
unique: A festival built around wild hogs, with a hog dog competition in the woods, barbecue by the plate and a street full of vendors in a town of 2,900.
buzz: The hog dog trials are the spectacle and draw handlers from across the state. It pulls thousands into Abbeville for a day.

name: Wilcox County Courthouse
unique: A 1903 Neoclassical courthouse by Frank Milburn at the crossroads of two federal highways, with a clock tower and a courtroom that still has the original gallery.
buzz: One of the better small county courthouses in this part of the state, and the square around it is intact. Ten minutes if you are passing through.

name: Rochelle Historic District
unique: A railroad town grid with a brick commercial block and a run of Victorian and Craftsman houses, listed as a district for holding together better than most towns its size.
buzz: Almost nobody stops, which is part of the appeal. The depot block and the churches are the buildings to see.

name: Copeland Strawberry Farms
customer: Families, bakers, people who want to pick their own
unique: A pick-your-own strawberry farm on the Wilcox County flatwoods, open daily in season with buckets provided and no frills beyond the fruit.
buzz: Cheap, sweet and quick, and the season is short. Call first because picking days depend on how much has ripened.

name: Fire Ant Festival
unique: Ashburn decided its worst pest was its best brand and built a whole festival on it, with a parade, a carnival, a 5K and a pageant named for the fire ant.
buzz: Thirty years in, it is the county's biggest weekend and the T shirts are the souvenir. Free to walk in, rides cost extra.

name: World's Largest Peanut
unique: A fiberglass peanut on a brick pedestal beside the interstate, put up to mark Ashburn as the home of the world's largest peanut processing plant.
buzz: It is a photo stop and nothing more, and people love it for exactly that. Easy off and back on I-75.

name: Ashburn Commercial Historic District
unique: A 1907 courthouse with a dome and a ring of early twentieth century storefronts around it, in a county carved out of four neighbors in 1905.
buzz: The courthouse is the anchor and the blocks around it are quiet enough to walk in twenty minutes. Pair it with the peanut and the festival grounds.

name: Wesleyan Methodist Campground and Tabernacle
dates: Year round, camp meeting in summer
unique: An open-sided tabernacle ringed by small wooden tents, the layout of a nineteenth century southern camp meeting ground that still holds its annual encampment.
buzz: A living survivor of a form that has mostly vanished. Visitors are welcome to walk it when services are not on.

name: Georgia Peanut Festival
unique: Sylvester calls itself the Peanut Capital of the World and closes the middle of town for two days of boiled peanuts, a parade and a recipe contest in Jeffords Park.
buzz: Boiled peanuts by the bucket and a hometown parade that fills the route. It is the county's homecoming more than a tourist event.

name: A&M Farms
customer: Families with young kids, school groups
unique: A Worth County row crop farm that opens its barnyard on weekends with inflatables, a petting zoo and a giant playground, plus u-pick fields in season.
buzz: Built for kids under ten and priced that way. Locals use it as the birthday party and Saturday morning default.

name: Historic Downtown Sylvester
customer: Walkers, shoppers, people passing on US 82
unique: A restored courthouse square that started as a railroad stop called Isabella Station, with the 1905 courthouse, brick storefronts and the peanut warehouses still standing at the tracks.
buzz: Small and tidy, with enough open businesses to make an hour of it. The depot end is the quietest and best preserved.

name: Little Ocmulgee State Park and Lodge
unique: A 265 acre lake with a sand beach, a nine hole course through the pines and a lodge built by the state in the 1930s, on ground that floods into cypress swamp at the north end.
buzz: The lake and the lodge make it the only real overnight stop for a wide stretch of south Georgia. Quiet midweek and full in summer.

name: Telfair Museum of History
unique: Displays on naval stores, timber rafting and the turpentine economy that built this county, plus record hunting and fishing trophies and photographs of the towns that no longer have a post office.
buzz: Appointment only, so call before you drive. Volunteers open it and will walk you through the timber trade the county was built on.

name: Peaches to the Beaches Yard Sale
unique: Georgia's longest yard sale strings out along US 341 for more than two hundred miles from the peach orchards to the coast, with Telfair County sitting in the middle of the run.
buzz: Two days of tables in fields and church parking lots. Dealers work it early, and the good furniture goes before nine on Friday.

name: General Coffee State Park
unique: A heritage farm inside a state park, with a log cabin village, a tobacco barn, farm animals and a boardwalk over the Seventeen Mile River swamp where gopher tortoises dig in the sandhills.
buzz: The farm is more interesting than the trails and people say so. The Burnham House cottage is the odd overnight option.

name: WWII Flight Training Museum
unique: One of the most intact of the 55 civilian pilot training fields from the war, with the original barracks, link trainer building and airfield, and about 10,000 pilots who learned to fly here before shipping out.
buzz: Volunteers who fly and restore the buildings run it, and the link trainer and the barracks rooms are the parts people remember. Small but real.

name: Broxton Rocks Preserve
dates: Guided visits by arrangement, spring and fall best
unique: A sandstone outcrop in the middle of flat pine woods with a seasonal waterfall, deep shaded crevices and tropical ferns and orchids growing where they have no business being this far north.
buzz: Access is limited and arranged in advance, which keeps it wild. People who go call the rock arch and the waterfall the surprise of south Georgia.

name: Georgia Blueberry Festival
unique: Fifty years of a festival in Georgia's blueberry capital, with fresh berries, a pie contest, a parade and a 5K at Goldwasser Park.
buzz: The berries sold at the park are picked that week and priced like a farm stand, not a festival. Go early before the flats run out.

name: Bacon Theatre
unique: A small town movie house that never closed for good, now showing films and hosting pageants, recitals and speakers under an old marquee on Alma's main street.
buzz: Tickets cost less than a soda at a chain, and the room is the point. The annual pageants fill it.

name: Alma-Bacon County Welcome Center
customer: Road trippers, people planning a county day
unique: A renovated 1920s school building staffed by local guides who will map a day of berry farms, the theatre and the swamp parks for you on paper.
buzz: Staffed by people who live there, which is worth more than the brochure rack. Ask for the farm stands that are actually picking that week.

name: Towns Bluff Park and Heritage Center
unique: A bluff over the Altamaha with a boardwalk through river swamp and a heritage center on the timber rafting and steamboat trade that used this river as a highway.
buzz: The yurts and the river view are the draw, and the museum is small but tells a trade nobody learns in school. Quiet on weekdays.

name: Bullard Creek Wildlife Management Area
unique: Seventeen thousand acres of Altamaha bottomland with cypress sloughs, sand ridges and a canoe route that puts you among alligators and nesting swallow-tailed kites.
buzz: Birders come for the kites in summer. The archery and shooting ranges make it a working management area, not a park.

name: The Big House
cost: Free to view, meals priced separately
unique: A 1914 Edwardian house on a rise over town that has been a family home, a restaurant and a guest house in turn, with the columns and the wide porch of a plantation house built sixty years after the war.
buzz: Locals point it out as the town landmark. Call before going, since its use has changed more than once.

name: Jeff Davis County Fair
unique: A county fair with livestock judging, canned goods and booth displays in the fairground building on Kirkland Still Road, the kind of fair that is judged by neighbours.
buzz: The livestock barn is the real event and the carnival is the add on. Cheap night out for a family.
